prompt: CFCs (e.g., CF₂Cl₂) deplete stratospheric ozone via radical chemistry. The first catalytic step involves:

options.label: UV photolysis releases Cl•, which then attacks O₃: Cl• + O₃ → ClO• + O₂
UV photolysis releases F• (weaker C-F bond), which attacks O₃: F• + O₃ → FO• + O₂
O₃ reacts directly with the intact CFC, abstracting a Cl to form ClO• + CF₂Cl•
Atmospheric water hydrolyzes CFC to HCl, which protonates O₃ into unstable HO₃

explanation: Stratospheric UV cleaves the WEAKEST C–X in a CFC — that's C-Cl (~81 kcal/mol), not C-F (~115). Cl• then catalytically destroys O₃: Cl• + O₃ → ClO• + O₂; ClO• + O → Cl• + O₂. One Cl atom can destroy ~10⁵ O₃ molecules before being removed.
